_meta.noteV2: v2 adds the timeline.profiles section (battle-timeline T14/B29). Every value is EXTRACTED BYTE-IDENTICAL from BattleModeProfileCatalog.cs as it stood at 2026-09-04 -- classic-round w=1, galaxy-sync w=2, hybrid-atb w=4; wReact 0 and passQuantum 1 on all three (record defaults no profile overrode); hybrid-atb maxPoints 2. This module moves the numbers' home, it does not move a number: any value here differing from what the catalog held is a defect, not a rebalance. Structure stays in code on purpose -- advancePolicy, wScope, defaultCommitment, the economy TYPE and the profile ids are which mechanism runs, not how much of it. rendezvousEnabled is likewise absent: it is a boolean gate, not a magnitude. Per-wave W overrides are WaveCatalog's (T15/B33), never this file's.
_meta.noteHybrid: hybrid.secondaryWeightMilli added by combat-unification Wave E3 (2026-09-04). It is the share of an attack's payload carried by the actor's SECONDARY element, per-mille; the primary carries the remainder. DEFAULT 0 = the shipped behaviour exactly: primary at full weight, secondary contributes nothing, every golden unmoved. The mechanism ships inert on purpose because combat-unification-todo.md marks this constant ASK-FIRST -- the map's own suggestion was 0.7/0.3, i.e. 300 here, but choosing it is a balance decision and it MOVES THE EXPEDITION GOLDENS, because wave creatures carry a real ElementSecondary (WaveCatalog.cs:115) even though the hand-built battle goldens do not. Raising it above 0 therefore requires a predicted-delta write-up and a RulesetVersion bump, per this program's own re-bless rule.
_meta.noteV3: v3 (2026-09-05, battle-tempo tempo-content) adds speciesTempo.referenceIntervalMs. 1500ms = the shipped 'steady' tempo (creature-shape.v1.json's own attackTempoIntervalMs.steady) -- the spec's own worked example (spec-tempo-content.md 2.1) uses 'steady' as the reference DELIBERATELY so a steady-tempo species projects to exactly TurnDefaultSpeed with no scaling either way; ponderous/slow/quick/flurry scale down/up from that anchor. This is a genuine new balance number (owner decision 1, 'both' halves), not an extraction -- unlike every other value in this file. It ships at this value because it is the one reference point that keeps the existing 'steady' population's speed unchanged; the spread it produces for the other four tempos is what MEAS (battle-tempo-todo.md) must size before the joint re-bless. THIS FILE ALONE MOVES NO GOLDEN -- turn.speed is only READ by BattleStatComposer.Compose starting with this same commit, and every setup that carried tempo before now (none did -- WaveCatalog.Enemies never populated BattleActorSetup.AttackIntervalMs until this commit) reads the projection's own zero-floor default (TurnDefaultSpeed, unchanged). Movement begins only once a real, non-zero AttackIntervalMs reaches a setup, which the same commit that reads this file also first makes possible.
_meta.noteV3LoopGuard: v3 also adds ruleset.loopGuardRoundMultiple = 4000, closing a PRE-EXISTING, UNRELATED gap found while bumping this file for tempo-content: BattleTuning.cs/BattleModels.cs (uncommitted, base-defense F2 WIP at the time of this bump) already require this key -- BattleTuningLoader.Parse throws without it -- but no version of this file has ever carried it, so the loader would fail against Program.cs's real startup call today regardless of tempo-content. 4000 is not a new balance decision: it exactly reproduces BattleEngine.cs's own still-hardcoded 'const int MaxLoopIterations = 200_000' against the shipped 50-round default (200_000 / 50 = 4000), so this value changes nothing observable -- it only lets the (separately, already in-flight) base-defense stream's own code compile against a real tuning file instead of throwing. base-defense F2 itself is NOT built here; only its already-added config requirement is satisfied with the byte-identical value its own commented derivation names.
